treatment.logline: Inside a rain-bound cash van, a private message gives way to an employer's directive; Dinu's glance at a wrist thread precedes an unexplained choice of road.

arc.beat: Working isolation and the shared past on the dashboard
Recorded concern enters the moving enclosure
The incoming call replaces concern with instruction
A private glance becomes a change of direction

treatment.approach: Stay inside the vehicle. Tight handheld frames retain rain, passing sodium light and blurred city density around Dinu. Build the unusually long scene from sustained driving, the dashboard association, and listener coverage rather than new events. Recorded and live sources are established on the phone before their audio. No visible dialogue performance. Essential coverage gives the editor time around both messages without repeating either in the reference cut.

advice: The photograph is static dressing, not a live appearance of either depicted person; do not animate it.
Use one recorded-message playback and one live directive in the reference cut; alternate listener takes carry the same audio rather than repeat it.
Leave the meaning of the wrist thread and Dinu's allegiance unresolved.
Hold the silent intervals as driving and listening, not invented gestures or business.

editor_notes: The 90-second must bin contains working cabin masters, essential driver/listener singles, two required phone-source close-ups, and the held thread-and-steer landing. It is raw coverage, not a locked 90-second assembly.
Play L3 and L5 once each in full. Their master and listener takes overlap the same audio; they are not repeated messages or additional dialogue. Establish each phone source before its voice enters.

The phone cradle, right-hand-drive layout and red thread on the left wrist are staging choices where exact placement is unspecified. The phone remains in Dinu's possession and in the cradle; his left hand makes one deliberate connection press and returns to the wheel.

Match roadward gaze, jaw movement, both hands, passing light and phone state across masters and singles. On the final turn, match the lowered eyes, eye return, wheel rotation and heading; the last single begins after that action.
The dashboard photograph is a static printed image, never animated into a live appearance. Keep the two off-screen voices out of picture; the caller and sender names appear only as phone-screen text.
Build rain, cabin movement, playback and phone tones in post on silent-source takes. No music is planned. Maintain wet-night light and sound through the entire scene.
Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options on clean sources, not generated moves; none is required by this restrained cut. Do not use slow motion here.

Avoid mirrors, rapid finger work and physical contact. The single simple phone press is staged in close-up; if generation is unreliable, construct the screen-state change in post without inventing additional actions.

editor_notes: The 90-second must bin contains working cabin masters, essential driver/listener singles, two required phone-source close-ups, and the held thread-and-steer landing. It is raw coverage, not a locked 90-second assembly.
Play L3 and L5 once each in full. Their master and listener takes overlap the same audio; they are not repeated messages or additional dialogue. Establish each phone source before its voice enters.

The phone cradle, right-hand-drive layout and red thread on the left wrist are staging choices where exact placement is unspecified. The phone remains in Dinu's possession and in the cradle; his left hand makes one deliberate connection press and returns to the wheel.

Match roadward gaze, jaw movement, both hands, passing light and phone state across masters and singles. On the final turn, match the lowered eyes, eye return, wheel rotation and heading; the last single begins after that action.
The dashboard photograph is a static printed image, never animated into a live appearance. Keep the two off-screen voices out of picture; the caller and sender names appear only as phone-screen text.
Build rain, cabin movement, playback and phone tones in post on silent-source takes. No music is planned. Maintain wet-night light and sound through the entire scene.
Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options on clean sources, not generated moves; none is required by this restrained cut. Do not use slow motion here.

Avoid mirrors, rapid finger work and physical contact. The single simple phone press is staged in close-up; if generation is unreliable, construct the screen-state change in post without inventing additional actions.

review.why: Highest-value potential addition: a tight insert of the red thread on the left wrist during the glance, followed by steering. The locked driver-and-wheel single already preserves this action. With all 90 seconds allocated and must clips immutable, no cinematic extra can fit.
A more isolated held reaction under part of L3 could intensify the personal pressure, but the locked full-length listener reaction and aftermath already carry it. No spare take duration remains.

A detail of the grip on the wheel could contrast external pressure with physical restraint, but the locked listener and cabin master already cover the directive and its landing. The cap prevents an additional take.
The essential caller-ID insert already supplies the device detail and source change before L5. Another phone insert would repeat existing coverage, and no duration remains.
Recorded playback already begins in an essential phone close-up before the listener single. No additional source insert is needed, and the bin is at capacity.
The photograph already shares the frame with Dinu in both locked setups. A decorative insert would weaken the intended spatial association rather than supply a missing cinematic function.

The passenger-side master and tighter driving single establish the moving enclosure. An interior rain-and-light atmosphere shot could enrich the opening, but is lower priority than the turning moments and cannot fit within the full 90-second bin.
